content: Individuals with diabetes are at a heightened risk of developing sensory impairments, including hearing loss. The prevalence of hearing loss in people with diabetes is approximately twice as high as in those without the condition. The underlying mechanisms proposed for this association include microangiopathy and auditory neuropathy, both of which are thought to result from chronic hyperglycemia and oxidative stress. Furthermore, diabetes has also been associated with impairments in taste and smell in certain cases.
